extra.message: The /evaluate endpoint passes the attacker-controlled request.form['expression'] value directly to eval(). An unauthenticated attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code

extra.message: The result of evaluating attacker-controlled input is concatenated directly into an HTML response without escaping. An expression returning attacker-supplied HTML or JavaScript causes reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The /lookup endpoint concatenates request.form['address'] into a shell command passed through rp() to os.popen(). Shell metacharacters allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary operating-system commands.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in an OS Command

extra.message: Attacker-controlled XML is parsed with DTD validation enabled and network access explicitly allowed. External entities can access local files or network resources, enabling XXE and server-side request forgery.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The /sayhi endpoint interpolates request.form['name'] into Jinja template source before calling render_template_string(). An attacker can inject Jinja expressions and reach arbitrary server-side code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: Attacker-controlled name input becomes literal template source rather than an escaped template variable. HTML and script elements are therefore returned unescaped, causing reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: The registration handler stores request.form['password'] directly in the User.password database column without hashing. A database disclosure would expose every user's plaintext password.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The /dashboard route performs no logged_in session check even though the application's home page treats dashboard functionality as authenticated content. Direct requests bypass the login gate and expose the vulnerable application functions.
The state-changing registration endpoint accepts POST requests without a CSRF token or origin validation. An attacker can cause a victim's browser to submit an unwanted account-registration request.
The /logout endpoint changes session state through an unprotected GET request. An attacker can force a logged-in user's browser to request this URL and terminate the user's session.
Flask debug mode is enabled while the development server listens on all interfaces. Unhandled exceptions can expose stack traces, source details, and the interactive debugger to remote clients.
